summary: Repository text supports a Go user-management backend with authenticated self-service profile, avatar, and external-identity operations; role-protected administrative user operations; PostgreSQL-owned user schemas; outbound file-storage, image-processing, and RBAC HTTP calls; and retained NATS request/reply contracts. The principal onboarding ambiguities are stale or mismatched OpenAPI and Taskfile content, unnamed connected-project mappings, unwired Tarantool/provider code, and administrative password handling after the auth-split migration.

facts.name: summary
facts.value: User-management Go microservice with HTTP and retained NATS RPC interfaces.
facts.evidence_quote: Production-ready Go microservice implementing user management with Clean Architecture, Echo, GORM, retained NATS RPC, and OAuth integrations.
facts.explanation: The README directly states the service purpose and major implementation approach.

open_questions.question: Should the checked-in OpenAPI auth paths be removed or moved to the authentication service?
open_questions.reason: docs/openapi.yaml defines /auth/signup, /auth/code-verification, and /auth/signin, but the production router in this repository mounts only internal health, user, and admin groups.

open_questions.question: Should the OpenAPI health and user paths be updated to match production route prefixes?
open_questions.reason: Production code mounts health below /internal and user routes below /api/v1/users, while the OpenAPI document describes /users/me and /users/{id} and does not describe /internal/health.

open_questions.question: Is the Taskfile run target stale?
open_questions.reason: Taskfile.yml runs ./cmd/ms-go-user, while the checked-in executable entry point is cmd/user-service/main.go and the Makefile runs ./cmd/user-service.

open_questions.question: Which connected project provides the configured file-storage endpoint?
open_questions.reason: Production configuration defaults to http://ms-filestorage:8000, but that runtime identifier does not exactly match any supplied connected-project name, so no relation fact can be established.

open_questions.question: Which connected project provides the configured image-processor endpoint?
open_questions.reason: Production code conditionally creates an image-processor HTTP client, but the repository does not identify its connected-project name in authoritative runtime text.

open_questions.question: Which connected project provides the RBAC HTTP and rbac.checkRole NATS contracts?
open_questions.reason: Production code identifies RBAC behavior and endpoints but does not directly identify an exact connected-project name in authoritative runtime text.

open_questions.question: Which connected project handles auth.verifyJWT?
open_questions.reason: Middleware delegates bearer-token verification through the configured NATS subject, but authoritative runtime text does not name an exact connected project.

open_questions.question: Is Tarantool still a runtime dependency?
open_questions.reason: A production Tarantool client exists and README describes two-step registration through Tarantool, but internal/app/app.go does not construct or wire that client.

open_questions.question: Is user_provider intentionally retained?
open_questions.reason: The migration creates user_provider and production code constructs its repository, but the constructed repository value is discarded and no production use case uses it.

open_questions.question: Should administrative password fields remain in this service after the auth split migration?
open_questions.reason: The auth-split migration drops user.password_hash, while administrative production code still hashes and assigns passwords to the domain object.

open_questions.question: Should checked-in seed migrations contain reusable credential hashes?
open_questions.reason: The seed migrations include password_hash values. No secret value is reproduced in this report, but user review is warranted because the later auth-split migration removes that column.

open_questions.question: Which CI system, if any, validates this repository?
open_questions.reason: No CI configuration was found among the inspected repository files.
